body.statement: Using \(\mathsf H_{\mathrm{LAN}}\), determine whether \(n\Psi_\infty(n)/\log n\) has a limit, characterize the sharp limit or sharp liminf and limsup over the fixed variance box, construct a logarithmic-batch schedule attaining the same sharp object, and decide whether the literal threshold \(B_{\mathrm{sat}}(n,2)\) is of order \(\log n\).
body.justification: Only a matched chronological constant can convert order-optimal saturation into the literal factor-two operational claim.
body.gap: Hirano and Porter characterize attainable sequential limits and Armstrong derives first-order efficiency bounds, but neither computes cumulative pre-update allocation loss or a saturation constant.
body.consumer: A sharp answer determines the smallest update count that is certifiably within a factor two of the best feasible cadence.

obligation.what_is_open: It remains to identify a sharp global limit or matching sharp liminf and limsup for \(n\Psi_\infty(n)/\log n\), to construct a logarithmic-batch design with the same leading constant uniformly over the variance box, and thereby to decide the upper bound \(B_{\mathrm{sat}}(n,2)=O(\log n)\).
obligation.obstruction: The exact score calculation yields a local coefficient on an interior fixed-scale path, but it does not justify passage to the global supremum over the compact variance box. In particular, a prior approaching \( (u,u)\) loses a fixed two-sided neighborhood, while an interior fixed prior has scale strictly below \(u\); neither supplies the conjectured boundary constant. A matching upper proof would also need sharp, rather than constant-factor, control of sequential variance estimation, exact-count rounding, and schedule optimization. The proved rate equivalence only yields logarithmic saturation for an unspecified sufficiently large factor and cannot certify factor two.
obligation.attempted: The early-kill fixed-scale calculation was carried out exactly, and a smooth-prior chronological information argument was used successfully for the rate lower bound. Extending that prior toward the upper corner makes its prior-information and boundary terms part of the leading-order problem; keeping it fixed leaves a strict scale gap. Separate local calculations and the current constant-factor plug-in schedule therefore do not match globally.
obligation.partial_result:
On the fixed-scale path \(\sigma_1(\theta)=se^\theta\),
\(\sigma_0(\theta)=se^{-\theta}\), the conditional score of each revealed Gaussian response is
\(\pm\{(Y-\mu_Z)^2/\sigma_Z^2-1\}\), with sign determined by the arm.  It has conditional variance exactly \(2\).  The parameter-free adaptive assignment kernels add no score, and martingale-score orthogonality therefore gives exact history information \(2T\) after \(T\) responses.  Near \(\theta=0\),
\(p^*(\theta)=(1+e^{-2\theta})^{-1}\), so \((p^*)'(0)=1/2\), while
\[
r_{\sigma(\theta)}(p)
=\frac{(\sigma_1(\theta)+\sigma_0(\theta))^2}{p(1-p)}
 \{p-p^*(\theta)\}^2.
\]
Thus the regular local information benchmark for estimating \(p^*\) is
\(1/(8T)\), and its quadratic allocation-loss benchmark at \(\theta=0\) is
\(2s^2/T\).  The proved rate theorem separately yields
\(\Psi_\infty(n)\asymp(\log n)/n\),
\(B_{\mathrm{sat}}(n,A)\asymp\log n\) for all sufficiently large fixed \(A\), and
\(B_{\mathrm{sat}}(n,2)=\Omega(\log n)\).
